profile.summary: ClinBench is a patient-level benchmark that Blank Bio assembled to evaluate checkpoints of its Ladon bulk RNA-seq foundation model: 142 survival, treatment-response and patient and tumour characteristic prediction tasks scored on frozen embeddings. It is described only in a section of the Ladon technical report, which uses it to relate pretraining loss to downstream performance. The task list, cohorts and splits are not published, so other groups cannot run it.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether embeddings from an RNA-seq foundation model carry information about patient outcomes and characteristics: survival, treatment response and patient and tumour characteristics. In the report it is used to test whether lower pretraining reconstruction loss goes with better downstream performance.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: 142 tasks: 85 within-cohort tasks, each scored by three-fold cross-validation repeated five times, and 57 cross-cohort survival tasks, where a model trained on the other cohorts of the same cancer type is tested on a held-out cohort; each held-out cohort counts as a separate task. The report does not list the tasks, cohorts, outcome definitions or patient counts.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each checkpoint's frozen embeddings feed elastic-net Cox models for survival and logistic regression for classification, with regularisation chosen by cross-validation on training data. Survival is scored by Harrell's concordance index and classification by AUROC, and the reported score is the unweighted mean over all 142 tasks. Four feature representations (raw, standardised, PCA 32, PCA 64) are tried per checkpoint and the one with the highest average score is reported. A gene-expression baseline uses the same tasks, splits and heads on log gene expression.
